title: Weak 'Soft Skills' Hurt Productivity, Employers Say
paragraphs: For a lot of work, technical knowledge is essential for getting things done. However, a survey of UK businesses has found that problems with communication, problem solving and other "soft skills" are getting in the way.
Workplace skill development company City & Guilds surveyed around 900 employers. It found that one in three UK businesses believes shortages in these skills are restricting productivity and growth.
Employers also reported that this soft skill shortage has led to low morale and increased staff turnover, as well as bad customer service.
The survey also found that nearly two-thirds of businesses feel that candidates with skills like good face-to-face communication, problem solving and time management are becoming harder to find.
As AI takes on more routine technical tasks for businesses, nearly three-quarters also said that these soft skills have, in fact, become more important than technical expertise for success at work.
At the same time, almost 70% worry that AI applicant screening tools, which are being used by an increasing number of employers, prioritize technical know-how over more human, soft skills.
City & Guilds also surveyed around 1,000 young British adults aged 18 to 24, asking how they feel about their skills and the job market.

It found that only two in five young adults feel completely confident in their face-to-face communication skills. Also, 17% said they don't feel confident presenting themselves professionally — although this rises to 34% among those who aren't already working, or are still in education.
More than half said they're worried that AI will reduce job opportunities for people their age.
That doesn't mean they aren't using AI to help themselves though — 41% said they're using it to improve both their work and communication skills.

City & Guilds' advice isn't to wait for young job applicants to learn soft skills by themselves, though. Instead, it advises that businesses train new staff in things like better communication when they join the company.
